best_architecture: Adopt MCP (Model Context Protocol) stdio transport as the polyglot bridge: each skill is a separate child-process MCP server that the host (Local-Claw nervous system) spawns and speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 to over stdin/stdout. This is the strongest pattern for a TS+Python+Rust skill mesh and is exactly how Local-Claw is already specced. Key design decisions, in priority order: (1) PROTOCOL AS CONTRACT, NOT ABI. MCP standardizes tool discovery (tools/list), invocation (tools/call), and JSON Schema input/output schemas over JSON-RPC 2.0 (the design is explicitly modeled on the Language Server Protocol). This makes language a pure implementation detail — a Rust skill and a Python skill are indistinguishable to the host because both expose the same JSON-RPC surface. Use each official SDK's native schema mechanism (Zod/Standard Schema in TS, Pydantic in Python, serde + schemars in Rust) and let it EMIT JSON Schema; never hand-author schemas, and never share a binary ABI across languages. (2) PROCESS ISOLATION OVER PLUGIN-IN-HOST. Running each skill as its own subprocess (vs. loading it into the host's address space like a classic dylib/plugin) gives crash isolation (a panicking Rust skill or a segfaulting native dep cannot take down the agent loop), independent dependency trees (no Python venv vs node_modules vs cargo conflicts), per-skill resource limits, and trivial polyglot support. The cost is per-call IPC serialization latency and process-spawn overhead — mitigate by keeping skill servers warm/long-lived (one persistent subprocess per skill, reused across calls) rather than spawning per invocation. This trade-off (isolation + polyglot vs. raw speed) is the central architectural call and process isolation is correct for an autonomous agent that loads untrusted-ish, heterogeneous skills. (3) SKILL DISCOVERY = MANIFEST FILE + REGISTRY, not blind filesystem scan. Each skill ships a small manifest (name, version, language, executable/command + args, env, declared capabilities) that the host reads to build a registry; MCP itself then provides runtime capability discovery via tools/list once the subprocess is launched. This two-tier model (static manifest for spawn config -> dynamic tools/list for actual tool schemas) mirrors the official modelcontextprotocol/registry (RESTful catalog over MongoDB) and the GitHub MCP Registry, and avoids fragile path-convention scanning. A filesystem scan can be a fallback to auto-populate the registry, but the manifest is the source of truth. (4) SECOND-TIER SANDBOX FOR UNTRUSTED RUST/COMPUTE SKILLS: WASM Component Model + WIT. For skills that need stronger sandboxing than OS process isolation (capability-based security, deterministic resource caps, portable single-artifact distribution), compile Rust skills to WASI Preview 2 components described by WIT interfaces and run them in Wasmtime, or use Extism (Wasmtime-based cross-language plugin framework) as a higher-level shim. This is a complementary inner layer: the skill is still presented to the agent as an MCP server, but the MCP server internally executes a WASM component (see hyper-mcp). Use this selectively — it adds a build/runtime layer, so reserve it for skills running model-generated or third-party code. (5) ONE HOST CLIENT, MANY TRANSPORTS-READY: build the host's MCP client so stdio is the default for local skills but the same client abstraction can later target Streamable HTTP for remote skills (Streamable HTTP replaced SSE as the recommended remote transport in spec 2025-03-26). NET: MCP-stdio child-process-per-skill + JSON-Schema-from-native-types + manifest/registry discovery + optional WASM/WIT inner sandbox is the recommended architecture; it directly maps onto Local-Claw's TS MCP server / Python MCP client / polyglot skill subprocess design.
reference_papers: A Survey of Agent Interoperability Protocols: Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent Communication Protocol (ACP), Agent-to-Agent Protocol (A2A), and Agent Network Protocol (ANP) (Ehtesham et al. 2025) - arxiv:2505.02279 - characterizes MCP as a JSON-RPC client-server interface for secure context ingestion and structured tool invocation; the canonical reference for choosing MCP over peer protocols

A Survey of AI Agent Protocols (Yang et al. 2025) - arxiv:2504.16736 - frames the pre-MCP fragmentation problem (every LLM/tool provider inventing proprietary invocation interfaces) that polyglot skill registries must solve; positions MCP as the standardizing layer / 'external brain' interface

ScaleMCP: Dynamic and Auto-Synchronizing Model Context Protocol Tools for LLM Agents (2025) - arxiv:2505.06416 - directly relevant to skill discovery/registry design: dynamic, auto-synchronizing tool registries for MCP, addressing how an agent discovers and keeps in sync a large, changing set of MCP tools

Unified Tool Integration for LLMs: A Protocol-Agnostic Approach to Function Calling (2025) - arxiv:2508.02979 - protocol-agnostic abstraction over function calling / tool protocols; useful for designing the host's skill-registry interface so it is not hard-coupled to one transport

The Evolution of Tool Use in LLM Agents: From Single-Tool Call to Multi-Tool Orchestration (2026) - arxiv:2603.22862 - surveys tool-use evolution and cites the MCP Specification (2025-06-18) as the standardization milestone; context for multi-skill orchestration [uncertain]

An Empirical Study of Agent Developer Practices in AI Agent Frameworks (2025) - arxiv:2512.01939 - empirical study of how developers actually structure tools/skills in LangChain/Semantic Kernel/AutoGen; useful evidence for registry/plugin design pitfalls [uncertain]

A Survey of the Model Context Protocol (MCP): Standardizing Context to Enhance Large Language Models (2025) - Preprints.org 202504.0245 - dedicated MCP survey covering the standardized framework for integrating LLMs with dynamic external systems (non-arxiv venue)
reference_repos: modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk - official TS SDK; MCP server + client libs, stdio + Streamable HTTP transports, Standard Schema (Zod v4/Valibot/ArkType) tool schemas - https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk
modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk - official Python SDK (the 'mcp' package); FastMCP-style server, stdio transport, Pydantic-based schemas - https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk

modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk - official Rust SDK (the 'rmcp' crate); macro-driven (#[tool_router], #[tool]) servers, transport::stdio, schemas derived from param structs; ~4.7M crates.io downloads - https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk

modelcontextprotocol/registry - official community registry; RESTful API for discovering/managing/publishing MCP servers, MongoDB + Docker (direct model for Local-Claw's manifest/registry + MongoDB memory) - https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry

modelcontextprotocol/servers - reference MCP servers (filesystem, git, fetch, memory/knowledge-graph) demonstrating the TS and Python SDKs; canonical skill-implementation examples - https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers

extism/extism - Rust-based cross-language WASM plugin framework on Wasmtime; PDKs for Rust/C/C++/Go/etc + host SDKs for Python/Go/etc; XTP Bindgen generates schema-driven bindings - https://github.com/extism/extism

joseph-wortmann/hyper-mcp - Rust MCP server that loads skills as sandboxed WebAssembly plugins; concrete reference for 'MCP server outside, WASM/WIT skill inside' layered sandbox - https://github.com/joseph-wortmann/hyper-mcp

bytecodealliance/wasmtime - reference WASM runtime implementing the Component Model + WASI Preview 2; runtime for sandboxed Rust skills compiled to WIT-described components - https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime

bytecodealliance/wasm-tools - wit-component / WIT tooling for authoring and composing WebAssembly components; defines the polyglot WIT interface contracts - https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasm-tools
intellectronica/skillz - MCP server for loading, discovering, and executing skills; small reference for a skill-discovery/registry MCP layer - https://github.com/intellectronica/skillz
wong2/awesome-mcp-servers - curated MCP server catalog (broad survey of skill implementations across languages) - https://github.com/wong2/awesome-mcp-servers
key_libraries: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk - TypeScript/Node.js - ^1.x (npm) - build TS skill MCP servers AND the host's MCP client; StdioServerTransport / StdioClientTransport for child-process bridge; Standard Schema tool I/O
mcp - Python - ^1.x (PyPI, 'mcp' package) - Python MCP client (Local-Claw's nervous-system client) and Python skill servers; stdio transport; integrates with Pydantic for JSON Schema
rmcp - Rust - latest crates.io (official modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk) - Rust skill MCP servers; macro-driven tool defs, transport::stdio, schemas auto-derived from param structs via schemars/serde
zod - TypeScript - ^4 (or Standard Schema: Valibot/ArkType) - define TS skill tool input/output schemas and emit JSON Schema as the cross-language contract
pydantic - Python - ^2 - define Python skill tool schemas; .model_json_schema() emits the JSON Schema contract consumed by the host registry
serde + serde_json + schemars - Rust - serde ^1, schemars ^0.8/^1 - serialize JSON-RPC payloads and derive JSON Schema for Rust skill tool params (the Rust side of the universal contract)
tokio - Rust - ^1 - async runtime backing rmcp stdio servers (AsyncRead/AsyncWrite over stdin/stdout)
wasmtime - Rust (also host SDKs in other langs) - ^2x/^3x series, WASI Preview 2 - runtime for executing Rust skills compiled to WASM Component Model components for capability-sandboxed execution
wit-bindgen - Rust + WIT toolchain - latest - generate guest bindings from WIT interface definitions so Rust skills implement the shared component contract
wasm-tools (wit-component) - Rust CLI/crate - latest - author, validate, and compose WIT-described WebAssembly components for polyglot sandboxed skills
extism + extism PDKs / XTP Bindgen - Rust host + per-language PDKs - Extism ^1.x - higher-level alternative to raw Wasmtime for cross-language WASM plugins with schema-driven bindings
jsonschema - Python (and ajv for TS) - latest - host-side validation of skill tool inputs/outputs against the JSON Schema advertised via tools/list
